page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 16 vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average category. Memory subsystem performance is notable, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top tier, and large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks placing in the top 25%. For compression workloads, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are strong, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression remains average.

In terms of workload execution, the server demonstrates strong text generation capabilities for small and medium language models, with 135M model text generation in the top tier and 7B model text generation in the top 25%. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput perform at average levels. Given the shared CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require high memory bandwidth and strong single-core bursts but do not demand sustained, dedicated multi-core execution. It is suitable for web serving, light database operations, and moderate text-based machine learning inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 16 shared vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and a 2.0 GHz clock speed. It features 32.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, with no GPU acceleration. Benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU and memory performance, alongside strong large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression speeds. Multi-core performance, database operations, and static web serving throughput align with average tiers. This hardware configuration is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, moderate database operations, and small-to-medium language model text generation, offering a balanced, cost-effective resource profile for non-dedicated compute needs.
